issues.jp_before: ぜひ今度[こんど]はお母[かあ]さんと一緒[いっしょ]に{買[か]いに来[き]てください|av-zehi}。
issues.problem: Distractor 買[か]いに来[き]るでしょう had a wrong reading for 来る (き instead of く), so it was malformed.
issues.action: Changed the distractor to 買[か]いに来[く]るでしょう.

issues.jp_before: {たとえ/どんなに|av-tatoe}友達[ともだち]に笑[わら]われても、私[わたし]は自分[じぶん]の意見[いけん]を変[か]えない。
issues.problem: Distractor もし is acceptable here: many native speakers say もし…ても for 'even if', which also fits the English.
issues.action: Replaced distractor もし with ぜひ.

issues.jp_before: {たとえ|av-tatoe}明日[あした]世界[せかい]が終[お]わるとしても、私[わたし]は友達[ともだち]を信[しん]じ続[つづ]けます。
issues.problem: Distractor もし is natural: もし明日世界が終わるとしても is a common set phrase with the same meaning.
issues.action: Replaced distractor もし with ぜひ.

issues.jp_before: {いくら/どんなに|av-tatoe}誘[さそ]われても、あの人[ひと]とは旅行[りょこう]に行[い]きたくない。
issues.problem: The English brought in an unstated 'he' and treated the inviter and 'that person' as two different people.
issues.action: Changed the English to 'No matter how often that person invites me, I don't want to go on a trip with them.'

issues.jp_before: いくら{謝[あやま]られても|av-tatoe}、あの日[ひ]の出来事[できごと]は忘[わす]れられない。
issues.problem: The English 'No matter how much I am apologised to' was unnatural.
issues.action: Changed the English to 'No matter how many times they apologise, I cannot forget what happened that day.'
